content: Use the CDN to load fonts, brand assets, motion components, and downloads across authorized SHAUGHV projects. Link the original asset instead of copying it into each app. These searchable docs are published at both cdn.shaughv.com and cdn.emmetts.dev. Use cdn.shaughv.com for current asset URLs; the older domain preserves its existing files. Public access does not grant redistribution rights. Open the visual website · Open the font guide Quickstart Paste one URL and start using fonts, marks, or packages. Fonts Makira + Paper Mono are standard. Gail Rock stays compatible; two other families are opt-in. Brand Wordmarks, favicons, and transparent figurines with live previews. Motion Browser-ready animated mark and loader drop-ins. What lives here Path What you get /fonts/ Family stylesheets plus web and desktop font files /brand/ Official wordmarks, favicons, and figurines /js/ Animated brand mark and loader custom elements /site/ The visual CDN website and font guide / This documentation; /docs redirects here If you do not know the filename, fetch /tree.json instead of guessing. It lists every hosted file with a paste-ready URL. How delivery works There is no application server in front of the files. Each object keeps the Content-Type and Cache-Control set by the static deployment. Binaries are immutable for a year. CSS and JavaScript use a one-day cache with a seven-day stale-while-revalidate window. Visual identity The website and these docs share the same cream, olive, and sage system. Cream 200: #F5F5F0 Sage: #5B8A5B Olive: #5C5446 Bamboo: #C4A876 Action: #4A7A4A Use the SVG from /brand/shaughv/logos/. Official SHAUGHV wordmark Standard type pair Makira and Paper Mono can both carry titles, interfaces, body copy, and buttons. Paper Mono is also the preferred monospace for code and data. Makira / sans One face. Any surface. Clear at reading sizes, forceful at display sizes, and comfortable on controls. Paper Mono / mono Same range. Fixed pitch. Expressive at display sizes, readable in body copy, and naturally precise for code. Load both families with one stylesheet: Next Start coding Copy the first working snippets. Recipes Common page setups for fonts, icons, and motion. Website layout How the public CDN pages are structured and how they reflow. Reference Namespaces, cache tiers, and discovery files.

content: The SHAUGHV type system is two versatile families, not a headline font plus a body font. Use either one for titles, display, interfaces, body copy, or buttons. Paper Mono also gives code and data a precise grid. Makira Standard sans. Weights 400–900, static and variable. Paper Mono Standard mono. Weights 100–800, static and variable. IBM Plex Mono Optional quieter mono with italics. Unbounded Optional geometric display family. Load the standard pair That one file imports Makira and Paper Mono, plus Gail Rock for compatibility with existing sites. The live manifest records the preferred pair in fonts.all.defaults. It does not import IBM Plex Mono or Unbounded. Family names Family Status CSS family names Weights Makira Standard "Makira", "Makira VF" 400–900 Paper Mono Standard "Paper Mono", "Paper Mono Variable" 100–800 Gail Rock Compatibility "Gail Rock", "Gail Rock VF" 100–700 IBM Plex Mono Opt-in "IBM Plex Mono" 100–700, italic Unbounded Opt-in "Unbounded", "Unbounded Blond", "Unbounded Variable" 300–900 + variable 100–900 Side by side The same sentence in both standard voices: Makira Ready for the whole interface. Clear at reading sizes, forceful at display sizes, and comfortable on controls. Paper Mono Ready for the whole interface. Expressive at display sizes, readable in body copy, and precise for code and data. Do not add another family to the standard bundle without an explicit brand decision. Opt-in stylesheets exist so a project can ask for a third voice on purpose. Recommended CSS variables The live font guide at visual font guide shows both families across display, body, interface, and control roles, plus Gail Rock's compatibility specimens.

title: Fonts

content: Paper Mono is the preferred monospace for new installations. Gail Rock remains in the combined stylesheet for existing designs. Gail Rock is a true monospace: every encoded glyph shares the same 650-unit advance. It is still a full interface family. Titles, body, buttons, and data can all wear it. The grid is a capability, not a restriction to code blocks. Display / 700 Make the headline count. Code preset / unmarked O + slashed zero const token = 0x00A0; font-family: "Gail Rock"; Load it Included in fonts/fonts.css. Solo import: CSS families Name Use "Gail Rock" Static 100–700 "Gail Rock VF" Variable 100–700 Static files on the CDN: Thin, Extralight, Light, Regular, Medium, Semibold, Bold. OpenType voices The grid never changes. Features switch the drawing of specific glyphs. Feature Effect Use default Unmarked O/o Body and the recommended code look ss01 Center-marked O/o, single-storey a/g, alternate Q/4 Signature display ss02 Slashed O/o and accented forms A sharper display voice zero Slashed numeral 0 Code and data dlig FI, LI, ft, tr ligatures Short display copy Choose ss01 or ss02 for expressive O forms, not both. zero and dlig can layer independently. Default O o · a g 4 Q O o a g 4 Q ss01 signature O o a g 4 Q ss02 slash O o Ó ó zero · capital O beside slashed 0 O 0 00A0 Best for code Keep the default, unmarked O/o and enable zero so numeral 0 cannot be confused with capital O. The feature name is literal: zero changes 0, while ss01 is the option that puts a center mark in O/o. The font guide at visual font guide includes a live weight-axis specimen and copyable CSS for every switch.

content: Makira is the versatile sans in the standard pair. It is not reserved for headlines. Use it anywhere the surface should feel owned without a fixed-pitch grid. Display / 700 One address. Every asset. Body / 400 Fonts, marks, favicons, figurines, and browser-ready motion for SHAUGHV projects. Link the exact thing you need. Use it anywhere. UI label / 700 Asset delivery / CDN Load it The standard bundle already includes Makira. A project that only wants this family can still link the dedicated file: CSS families Name Use "Makira" Static cuts, 400–900 "Makira VF" Variable 400–900 Files on the CDN fonts/makira/ makira.css woff2/ — browser-first webfonts woff/ ttf/ otf/ variable/ — "Makira VF" Static filenames follow Makira-Regular.woff2, Makira-Medium.woff2, Makira-SemiBold.woff2, Makira-Bold.woff2, Makira-ExtraBold.woff2, and Makira-Black.woff2. If a cut ever needs a hint regen or a glyph addition, ship a new filename. Binary objects are cached as immutable. Never overwrite Makira-Bold.woff2 in place. License Makira is commercially licensed for authorized SHAUGHV use. Public font URLs do not grant permission to redistribute its binaries. Use the hosted CSS rather than committing it to public repositories.

content: The standard stylesheet stays focused on Makira and Paper Mono. These two families are fully hosted, but each has its own CSS file. IBM Plex Mono A quieter optional mono for technical labels, code, and dense metadata. Normal and italic, 100–700. IBM Plex Mono / 700 IBM Plex Mono status: ready · GET /tree.json Paper Mono remains the standard code face. content: Paper Mono is the default monospace for new SHAUGHV projects. Pair it with Makira for labels, code, data, interfaces, and display text. Paper Mono / 700 Make the headline count. const token = 0x00A0; Install The combined stylesheet includes the preferred Makira + Paper Mono pair. Gail Rock remains included for compatibility with existing designs; fonts are downloaded only when used. For Paper Mono alone: Files and weights Build Formats Weights CSS family Static WOFF2, TTF, OTF 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800 "Paper Mono" Variable WOFF2, TTF Continuous 100–800 "Paper Mono Variable" All 26 supplied font files are hosted without changing their bytes. The variable filenames are normalized to PaperMono-Variable. Normal style is supplied; there is no separate italic. Printable ASCII has fixed advances. Combining marks and some extended glyphs have different advances, so check your actual content when exact columns matter. License and discovery Paper Mono uses the SIL Open Font License 1.1. The OFL, copyright notice, and verified metadata accompany the font files. Use fonts["paper-mono"] in the live catalog for the current stylesheet and fonts.all.defaults for the recommended pair. The visual font guide includes an interactive variable-weight specimen. OpenType features The supplied variable font includes zero, calt, frac, ss01–ss04, cv01, and other tags recorded in its metadata. Enable the slashed-zero option with font-feature-settings: "zero" 1. Stylistic-set meanings are specific to Paper Mono; do not reuse Gail Rock's alternate-glyph descriptions for it. Choosing a format Use the family stylesheet for browsers; it prefers WOFF2. Use TTF or OTF for compatible desktop software, retaining the license notices. Choose the variable family when a design needs intermediate weights such as 450. To avoid synthetic italics, set font-synthesis: none where the absence of an italic face matters, or explicitly choose an italic-capable family.

content: Two domains, one documentation source Host Role Hosting cdn.shaughv.com Current asset catalog and documentation Vercel static deployment cdn.emmetts.dev Documentation mirror and preserved legacy assets GitHub Pages Both homepages publish the same Blume build. Current font, brand, motion, and download examples use cdn.shaughv.com. The older domain keeps its existing asset paths, but it is not a second copy of the current catalog. The primary CDN uses Vercel DNS and managed HTTPS. The documentation mirror keeps its existing DNS and GitHub Pages custom domain. No runtime function, database, or Blob store is required. The original R2 bucket is a historical snapshot, not the current origin or a synchronized backup. Free hosting boundaries The primary site uses Vercel Hobby. Its transfer and request allowances are shared with other projects on the account; they are not unlimited. Check Vercel's current plan documentation before changing the audience or increasing traffic. GitHub Pages applies its own service limits to the mirror. No paid subscription was added for this setup. Documentation follows repository changes The private RealEmmettS/shaughv-cdn repository is the canonical source for assets, the catalog, and the Markdown/MDX pages. Blume is pinned in the lockfile. Its build produces navigation, local search, page HTML, Markdown exports, agent discovery, social images, and the sitemap together. Every change must update affected documentation before it is pushed. The repository's agent instructions require checking URLs, font defaults, examples, and workflows, followed by the docs build and strict link validation. GitHub CI checks the same build. There is no scheduled AI maintenance job. On Windows, run the shell commands through Git Bash. The public preview uses python3 scripts/serve-site.py after the build and binds to localhost. Publishing both hosts Deploy the complete public package to a Vercel preview and verify it before publishing production. Then use the repository's Pages publisher to copy the same compiled documentation into the existing RealEmmettS/Shaughnessy-CDN checkout. Push its main branch to trigger GitHub Pages. The publisher preserves legacy assets and CNAME, tracks the generated files it owns, and removes obsolete generated files on subsequent updates. Fonts are loaded from their canonical CDN URLs rather than copied into the public mirror. Private source and maintenance files are excluded from both outputs. Verification and recovery Check rendered pages, search, navigation, mobile layout, and actual font loading. The primary CDN's live verifier also checks exact file bytes, response types, cache policy, CORS, downloads, byte ranges, missing files, and cache hits. HTTP success alone does not prove that a font rendered or a search result works. For a broken Vercel release, roll back to a previously verified deployment. For a broken Pages update, revert the publishing commit and wait for the Pages build to finish. Preserve immutable asset URLs: changed binary files need new filenames because a deployment cannot clear a visitor's browser cache.
description: Where the two CDN domains run, how the documentation stays current, and how to validate a change.
title: Hosting and updates

content: Two browser-ready custom elements cover the animated wordmark loop and the official loader. Both inherit currentColor and skip motion when the visitor asks for less of it. Animated brand mark js/animated-brand-mark.js defines <shaughv-mark>. The loop is: Wordmark holds Undraws Portrait (mustache + glasses) draws in Undraws Wordmark returns Hold a static frame with data-static (the footer of the CDN website does this): A React source port also ships at js/react/AnimatedBrandMark.jsx for projects that already own the component tree. The vanilla custom element is the default for HTML pages. Color comes from CSS. Set color on the host. Do not recolor individual SVG paths. Loader js/shaughv-loader.js defines <shaughv-loader>. The portrait fills, drains, and morphs through a goo filter into a blob, then returns. Timing, paths, and geometry are part of the recipe. The loader will fetch Anime.js from jsDelivr if the page has not already loaded it. The CDN website loads Anime.js itself so the mark choreography and the loader share one copy. Reduced motion Both drop-ins honor prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. The mark stays on the static wordmark. The loader does not run the morph loop. Keep that behavior if you wrap either element. Live preview The homepage Assets section mounts both elements against cream stages so you can confirm color inheritance before copying the snippet. Open the Assets section

content: Blume 2.2.2 powers the documentation homepage on both CDN domains, with local search, navigation, Markdown exports, and agent discovery. The original visual guides remain available separately as two HTML pages plus shared CSS and JS: site/ index.html — CDN overview fonts.html — complete typography guide site.css — layout, type, breakpoints site.js — nav, copy buttons, motion, reveals Both pages share the header, cream field, sage accents, and Paper Mono display titles. Catalog labels on the homepage use Makira so four columns stay one family instead of four competing mono letterforms. Header Links: Fonts, Assets, Downloads, Docs, and the Start coding action. Below 960px the bar collapses to a 44px hamburger with keyboard dismiss, outside click, and Escape. Open the visual overview to confirm the Docs item lands on these pages. Homepage catalog The "Four ways in." section is a four-column grid on wide screens and two columns below 1280px. Each card is a container: the title scales from the card width (cqi) so TYPE, IDENTITY, MOTION, and PACKAGES stay inside the rules at every width. Width Catalog ≥ 1280px Four columns 481px–1279px Two columns ≤ 480px One column Cell borders are right + bottom on every card, so changing the column count never leaves a missing or doubled rule. Other reflow points Width What changes 1080px Hero stacks, section headings stack, font-brief stacks 960px Header becomes a menu 760px Asset grids, specimens, downloads, and footer stack 480px Hero actions stretch, receipt chrome stacks, catalog is one column Display titles use overflow-wrap and text-wrap: balance so long Paper Mono words wrap inside the measure instead of painting through the next column. Preview locally Check the visual overview and font guide at 1440, 1280, 1024, 768, and 390. The catalog, hero receipt, and font specimens are the places overflow used to show up first. Screenshots from those widths belong next to this page when a pass is captured during review. The live pages remain the source of truth. Shared asset cache markers site/index.html and site/fonts.html load site.css and site.js with the first 12 characters of each file's SHA-256 as ?v=. Tests fail if a marker drifts after an edit.
